title: Juan Tizol and his compositions Caravan and Perdido
summary: Rooming with Tizol and Tricky Sam in theaters, Brown saw Tizol work out Caravan, and lists his Latin-flavored tunes.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Who were some of the other composers or people whose music was incorporated frequently?
Well, there was Tizol. I think I told you of Tizol.

Oh, definitely. And we were playing theaters at that time, and in the theaters, the trombones usually had a room together, and the saxes had a room together -- you know like that. So, Tizol and Tricky and I -- we roomed together. And Tizol was very anxious to get this

number on. And we used to try to figure out -- he couldn't remember exactly he'd like for the middle to go. And so, he'd make eight bars of extemporaneous playing in the middle and come back to the eight bars in the end. And -- but he wrote it.
Uh-huh. And didn't he also write Perdido 'Fredita'?

Yes, he wrote "Perdido", he wrote -- he has about eight tunes of the Latin flavor, and they were very nice, very nice tunes. But after so long, you can't remember or you lose track of where they go or what's happening to them.
